name: Photocopy Art / Zine Design
visualIdentity: Supplemental reference, not a directly named source-collection style. High-contrast photos, photocopy grain, torn edges, cutout headlines, tape or staples, and irregular page layouts create a raw handmade collage. Keep one information center and lettering readable.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to activist explainers, DIY guides, community announcements, band promos, lyric zines, and music event recaps when paired with annotations or beat-timed page changes. More broadly, its editorial collage can support video or interactive storytelling; that wider suitability is inferred.
limitations: Avoid body copy in handwriting, covering faces, adding a third ink color, or letting collage obscure the focal point. Omit or adapt pinned, stacked, or chaptered motion if it harms page layout, hides needed content, crops details, or adds spectacle without explanation. These are design constraints, not claims about universal performance.
palette: Suggested new-art palette: white (#FFFFFF) background, black (#000000) foreground, and optional red (#BF3232) accent; omit red for monochrome. These are suggestions, not canonical colors. Preserve supplied or approved colors, semantic roles, source artwork, and color-family/count limits. Use discrete tokens with no gradients; check actual text contrast over composited imagery and textures.
motionAndInteraction: Animate deliberate pasting, page turns, and recomposition while preserving readable holds; grain stays fixed. Optional music pairing uses verified downbeats, not every element, and avoids full-frame flashing. Interactive HTML may use scroll progress to recompose a pinned hero, reveal stacked cards, hand off chapters, or advance story states. Keep the outer hero stable, release pins without jumps, preserve backward states, keyboard/touch and reduced-motion behavior. These patterns are optional and scene-dependent.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, narration, effects, ambience, vocals, or silence for the topic and user requirements. If beat-locked, use verified beats and preserve headline reading holds; do not assume assets exist. Keep speech clear and inspect synchronization and mix.
assetRequirements: Prepare high-contrast imagery, fixed grain, torn-edge treatments, cut lettering, and page layers; use preprocessing/compositing tools such as Pillow or Sharp where useful. Exact copy, photos, fonts, aspect ratio, and audio assets are unspecified. Keep assets deterministic and separate visual construction from composition/export.
combinations: Pair with style-024 marker annotations for black or optional red arrows/circles guiding one focal point; use readable type for longer copy. Pair with style-105 beat timing for music-led pastes, using verified beats and fixed grain. These combinations are explicit suggestions; other style combinations are unspecified and should preserve the one-center, limited-ink rules.
productionApproach: Choose visual renderer and motion engine for style fidelity first; assign each animated property one owner. Preprocess and composite pages, then expose deterministic states by seekable time or baked assets. HyperFrames is the primary composition/export pipeline; Remotion only if unavailable or a verified required capability is blocked, with reason recorded. Neither defines the visual treatment. For interactive HTML, map scroll to progress; do not make video depend on live input. Validate representative frames, text, transitions, audio sync, and final playback.
